entry: Largest island of the Windward group of the Society Islands in [[French Polynesia]] (pop., 2017: 189,517). It is made up of two roughly circular land masses, Tahiti Nui and Tahiti Iti, joined by an [[Isthmus]]; both are eroded remnants of extinct [[Shield volcano|shield volcanoes]]. The island lies in the central [[Pacific Ocean]], and its beaches and coral reefs support tourism and fishing. The capital of French Polynesia, Papeʻete, is on the island's northwest coast. Polynesians settled the island between 900 and 1100 CE. France annexed it in 1880, and French is the sole official language, though Tahitian is widely spoken.

Special municipality in central [[Taiwan]] and the island's second-largest city, with more than 2.86 million residents. Located in the Taichung Basin, it grew from scattered hamlets of Taiwanese indigenous peoples who lived by cultivating [[Millet|millet]] and [[Taro|taro]]. The Qing renamed the settlement Taiwan-fu between 1887 and 1894, when it was planned as the provincial capital, but the capital was moved to [[Taipei]]. Japanese planners developed the modern city from 1895. On 25 December 2010 the former provincial city merged with Taichung County to form the special municipality. The city is home to the National Museum of Natural Science, the National Taichung Theater and the historic Taichung Park.

Biome of [[Conifer|coniferous]] forests dominated by [[Pine|pines]], [[Spruce|spruces]] and larches, also called boreal forest. It is the world's largest land biome, covering 17 million square kilometers (6.6 million square miles), or 11.5% of Earth's land area. In North America it covers most of inland Canada and Alaska. In Eurasia it extends across Sweden, Finland, much of Russia including most of [[Siberia]], and parts of northern Mongolia and Japan's Hokkaido. The taiga in its current form has existed only for the last 12,000 years, since the start of the [[Holocene]] epoch. Apart from the permanent ice caps and [[Tundra]], it has the lowest annual average temperatures of any terrestrial biome, and winters below freezing last 5–7 months. [[Climate change]] threatens it, and how the carbon dioxide it absorbs or emits should be counted in carbon accounting is controversial.

New Zealand filmmaker and actor. His features *Boy* (2010) and *Hunt for the Wilderpeople* (2016) were each the top-grossing film entirely funded and produced in New Zealand. He directed, wrote and starred in the black comedy *Jojo Rabbit* (2019), which won the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay, and directed the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] film *Thor: Ragnarok* (2017). He co-wrote and co-directed the horror comedy *What We Do in the Shadows* (2014) and co-created the series *Reservation Dogs*. [[Time (magazine)|Time]] named him one of the 100 most influential people in the world in 2022.

Capital and special municipality of [[Taiwan]] (pop., March 2023: 2,494,813). Taipei lies in northern Taiwan on the Taipei Basin, an ancient lakebed. Taipei has been the island's political center since 1887, when it became the seat of Taiwan Province under the [[Qing dynasty]]. From 1895 to 1945 it was the seat of the Japanese Government-General, known as Taihoku. It has been the national seat of the Republic of China government since 1949, and it became a special municipality on 1 July 1967. It is Taiwan's economic, political, educational and cultural center. Its landmarks include Taipei 101, formerly the tallest building in the world, the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall and the National Palace Museum. Because of Taiwan's ambiguous international status, the term Chinese Taipei is often used for the country at international organizations and sporting events, including the Olympics.

Civil war in late imperial China (1850–1864) between the [[Qing dynasty]] and the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. Led by [[Hong Xiuquan]], an ethnic Hakka who proclaimed himself the younger brother of [[Jesus|Jesus Christ]], the movement sought to convert the Han people to a syncretic Christianity and to overthrow the Qing. Taiping armies occupied much of the middle and lower [[Yangtze]] valley, and the kingdom based in [[Nanjing]] ruled nearly 30 million people at its peak. Estimates of deaths range from 20 to 30 million up to 73–100 million, and it was the deadliest civil war in history. Zeng Guofan's Xiang Army besieged Nanjing; Hong died during the siege in June 1864, and the city fell about a month later. The war weakened the Qing state and accelerated the rise of provincial powers.

Country in East Asia, officially the Republic of China, comprising the island of Taiwan and nearby islands in the northwestern Pacific. Large-scale Han Chinese immigration began under Dutch rule in the 17th century. The island was annexed by the [[Qing dynasty]] in 1683 and ceded to the [[Empire of Japan|Japanese empire]] in 1895. After Japan's surrender in [[World War II]], the Republic of China, led by [[Chiang Kai-shek]] and the [[Kuomintang]], assumed control; its government moved to Taiwan in 1949 after the loss of mainland China in the [[Chinese Civil War]]. Rapid growth from the early 1960s, known as the Taiwan Miracle, was followed by a transition to multiparty democracy in the late 1980s and early 1990s. Its status is contentious: the People's Republic of China claims it, and UN members recognized the PRC instead of the Republic of China in 1971.

Strait about 180 kilometers (110 mi) wide, separating [[Taiwan]] from mainland [[Asia]]. It connects the [[South China Sea]] to the south with the [[East China Sea]] to the north, and its narrowest point is 126 km (78 mi) wide. The strait lies on Asia's [[Continental shelf|continental shelf]] and is almost entirely less than 150 m (490 ft) deep, with many islands, including [[Kinmen]] and Penghu. It separates [[Fujian]] Province from Taiwan. Its former names include the Formosa Strait. An informal median line, defined in 1955 by US Air Force general Benjamin O. Davis Jr., never gained official status, and the People's Republic of China has never recognized it. In 2019 warplanes of the [[People's Liberation Army]] crossed the median line.

Capital of Shanxi Province in northern China (pop., 2021: 5,390,957). Taiyuan is the political, economic and cultural center of the province, with an industrial base focused on energy and heavy chemicals. It lies roughly in the center of Shanxi on the Fen River. Its first city, Jinyang, was built in 497 BC, and the city has more than 2,500 years of urban history. It was the capital or provisional capital of many dynasties, which gave it the name Lóngchéng, meaning City of the Dragon. The [[Qin dynasty|Qin]] state took the area in 248 BC, and from 221 BC it was a commandery of the first imperial dynasty, with Jinyang as its seat. Under the [[Sixteen Kingdoms]] it was part of several short-lived states. Its status as a northern capital in the Tang and Five Dynasties gave it the names Běidū and Běijīng, different from present-day [[Beijing]].

Ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the [[Yamuna]] River in [[Agra]], [[Uttar Pradesh]], India. [[Shah Jahan]], the fifth [[Mughal Empire|Mughal]] emperor, commissioned it in 1631 as the tomb of his wife, Mumtaz Mahal; he is also buried there. The mausoleum was completed in 1648, and the complex was believed finished in 1653. White marble inlaid with semi-precious stones forms the mausoleum, while red [[Sandstone]] was used for other buildings. More than 20,000 workers and artisans were employed under a board of architects led by Ustad Ahmad Lahori, the emperor's court architect. It is regarded as one of the best examples of Mughal architecture. UNESCO designated it a [[World Heritage Site]] in 1983, and it attracts more than five million visitors a year.

Landlocked country in [[Central Asia]], bordered by [[Afghanistan]], [[Uzbekistan]], [[Kyrgyzstan]] and [[China]]. Its capital, Dushanbe, is its largest city, with over 1.2 million people. Mountains cover more than 90% of the country. Tajikistan declared independence from the [[Soviet Union]] on 9 September 1991, and a civil war followed from May 1992 to June 1997. Emomali Rahmon has led it since 1994, and his authoritarian regime has been criticized for its human rights record. Tajiks form the ethnic majority, and Tajik is the national language, with Russian used as the official inter-ethnic language. Islam is nominally adhered to by 97.5% of the population. The developing economy relies on remittances and on [[Aluminium|aluminum]] and [[Cotton|cotton]] production.

Desert in northwestern [[China]], covering 337,000 square kilometers (130,000 sq mi), slightly smaller than Germany. It lies in the Tarim Basin of southern [[Xinjiang]] and is bounded by the [[Kunlun Mountains]] to the south, the Pamir Mountains to the west, the [[Tian Shan]] to the north and the [[Gobi Desert]] to the east. Two branches of the [[Silk Road]] crossed its northern and southern edges, and travelers avoided its arid wasteland. Dunes rise from 60 feet (18 m) to as much as 300 feet (91 m), and sandstorms are dangerous. Settlement is usually limited to [[Oasis|oases]]. In 1978 China launched the Green Great Wall project, and by 2024 a 3,050-kilometer (1,900-mile) green belt had been completed around the desert. Folk etymology gives the name as Place of No Return.

Turkish politician, chairman of the Union and Progress Party and Grand Vizier from 1917. An early member of the Committee of Union and Progress (CUP), he became Minister of the Interior after the 1908 Young Turk Revolution. In 1913 he and [[Enver Pasha]] carried out a coup, and as civilian leader of a triumvirate he was the de facto ruler of the [[Ottoman Empire]] until 1918. He brought the empire into [[World War I]] and negotiated the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with the Bolsheviks. He is widely considered the main perpetrator of the [[Armenian genocide]]; on 24 April 1915 he ordered the arrest of Armenian intellectuals, and he is held responsible for the death of around 1 million Armenians. In November 1918 he fled the country, and an Ottoman tribunal sentenced him to death in absentia. He was assassinated in Berlin by Soghomon Tehlirian, a member of the Armenian Revolutionary Federation.

Soft clay mineral of hydrated magnesium silicate, Mg₃Si₄O₁₀(OH)₂. Powdered talc, often combined with corn starch, is used as baby powder. It serves as a thickening agent and lubricant and is an ingredient in [[Ceramic|ceramics]], [[Paint|paints]] and roofing material, and it is a main ingredient in many [[Cosmetics]]. Talc is the softest mineral, ranking 1 on the [[Mohs scale]] of hardness, and it is insoluble in water. It forms mainly through the metamorphism of magnesian minerals such as [[Olivine|olivine]] and serpentine. Soapstone is a [[Metamorphic rock|metamorphic rock]] composed mostly of talc. Some epidemiological studies associate perineal use of cosmetic talc with a modest increase in ovarian cancer risk, but reviews cite limitations of that evidence, and regulators require [[Asbestos|asbestos]] testing of talc products.

American sociologist of social action theory and structural functionalism. He taught at [[Harvard University]] from 1927 to 1973 and was one of the first professors in its new sociology department in 1930. Parsons translated [[Max Weber]]'s work and analyzed the writings of Weber, [[Émile Durkheim]] and [[Vilfredo Pareto]]. His social action theory, based on empirical data, is described as the first broad, systematic and generalizable theory of social systems developed in the United States and Europe. Although generally considered a structural functionalist, in 1975 he argued that those terms did not describe his theory. From the 1970s, a new generation of sociologists criticized his theories as socially conservative and his writing as overly complex. He was elected president of the American Sociological Association in 1949 and promoted the professionalization of sociology.

Sunni Islamist political and militant organization in [[Afghanistan]]. Emerging during the Afghan civil war in 1994, the Taliban captured [[Kabul]] in 1996 and ruled until the [[United States|United States]]-led invasion that followed the [[September 11 attacks]] in 2001. It returned to power in 2021. Its government enforced a strict interpretation of [[Sharia]] and has been condemned for civilian massacres, human rights abuses and restrictions on women. Its ideology draws on the Deobandi movement and Pashtun nationalism. It has been designated a terrorist organization by several countries, and as of 2026 [[Russia]] is the only state to have granted it diplomatic recognition.

Genre of television, radio and podcast programming built around spontaneous [[Conversation|conversation]]. A host guides discussion with guests, who may be experts or non-experts, while a studio or call-in audience takes part. The host's personality shapes the tone of the show. A common convention is fresh talk, meaning talk that is spontaneous or seems so. Talk shows originated in the [[United States]] and discuss social, political or religious issues and events. Subgenres include early morning chat shows, daytime tabloid programs, self-help shows such as *The Oprah Winfrey Show*, evening panel discussions, late-night comedy shows with monologues and celebrity interviews, and Sunday morning political programs. Talk shows are produced at low cost and are typically not aired during prime time.

American rock band formed in [[New York City]] in 1975. David Byrne, Chris Frantz, Tina Weymouth and Jerry Harrison helped pioneer new wave by mixing punk, art rock, [[Funk|funk]] and world music. Working with producer [[Brian Eno]], they recorded *Remain in Light* (1980). *Speaking in Tongues* (1983) brought mainstream success, and the concert film *Stop Making Sense* (1984) is often regarded as the greatest concert film of all time. Byrne left in 1991, and the band disbanded after releasing *No Talking, Just Head* in 1996. The band was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2002.

Capital city of [[Florida]] and county seat of Leon County. It became the capital of the Florida Territory in 1824 and is the largest city in the Florida Panhandle, with an estimated 205,089 residents in 2024. Florida State University, Florida A&M University and Tallahassee State College make it a college town with more than 70,000 students. The name is a Muskogean word often translated as old fields. In 1539–40 [[Hernando de Soto]]'s expedition wintered in the Apalachee town of Anhaica, where the encampment is often cited as the first place [[Christmas]] was celebrated in the continental United States.

Capital and largest city of [[Estonia]] (pop., 2026: 452,563), on the shore of the Gulf of Finland, part of the [[Baltic Sea]]. It is the country's main governmental, financial, industrial and cultural center, located 80 kilometers (50 mi) south of [[Helsinki]]. From the 13th to the early 20th century it was known in most of the world as Reval. Reval received Lübeck city rights in 1248, and in the 14th to 16th centuries it became the northernmost member city of the [[Hanseatic League]]. Tallinn Old Town is one of the best-preserved medieval cities in Europe and a [[World Heritage Site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]]. The city was the birthplace of [[Skype]] and Bolt, and it hosts the headquarters of the [[European Union]]'s IT agency and the [[NATO]] Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence.

Central text of Rabbinic [[Judaism]], a primary source of Jewish law and theology. It consists of the Mishnah and its commentaries, the Gemara, and records the teachings and disagreements of thousands of [[Rabbi|rabbis]]. The text has 63 tractates and is written in [[Aramaic]] and Hebrew. It was compiled between the destruction of the Second Temple in 70 CE and the early seventh-century Arab conquest. The Babylonian Talmud is the more extensive and authoritative version, and the word usually refers to it. In Rabbinic Judaism it is second in authority only to the [[Hebrew Bible]]. Until the Haskalah in the 18th and 19th centuries, it was the centerpiece of Jewish culture in nearly all communities. Opinions based on the Jerusalem Talmud reached the Mishneh Torah of [[Maimonides]].

Queen of Georgia (r. 1184–1213), known as Tamar the Great. A member of the Bagrationi dynasty, she was crowned co-ruler by her father, George III, in 1178 and became the first woman to rule Georgia in her own right. Medieval Georgian sources gave her the title mepe, or king. Her reign presided over the apex of the Georgian Golden Age, and her empire dominated much of the [[Caucasus]] until Mongol attacks brought its collapse within two decades of her death. Her first husband, Yury Bogolyubsky, was divorced and expelled from the country. Her second husband was David Soslan, and their children, George and Rusudan, both became monarchs of Georgia. She is an idealized figure in Georgian arts, and the Georgian Orthodox Church canonized her as a [[Saint|saint]].

Leguminous tree, *Tamarindus indica*, bearing edible [[Fruit|fruit]]. It is indigenous to tropical Africa, naturalized in Asia and the only species in its genus, which belongs to the family [[Fabaceae]]. The brown, pod-like fruit has a sweet, tangy pulp used in cuisines worldwide, in [[Traditional medicine|traditional medicine]] and as a [[Dye|dye]]. Its young leaves are used in Indian and Filipino cuisine, and seed oil can be extracted from the seeds. The wood is used for [[Woodworking]]. The pulp flavors sauces such as [[Worcestershire sauce]]. The crown can reach 25–30 meters (82–98 feet), and a mature tree may produce up to 225 kg (496 lb) of fruit a year. Because of its many uses, it is cultivated throughout tropical and subtropical zones. The name derives from an Arabic phrase meaning Indian date.

Southernmost state of [[India]], with [[Chennai]] as its capital and largest city. It is the home of the Tamils, who speak [[Tamil language|Tamil]], the state's official language. The state lies between the [[Western Ghats]] and the [[Bay of Bengal]], and it shares an international maritime border with [[Sri Lanka]] at Pamban Island. Tamil Nadu has more than 5,500 years of continuous cultural history. Manufacturing accounts for nearly one-third of the state's GDP, and its economy ranks second among India's 28 states. Its tourism industry is the largest of any Indian state, drawing on four [[World Heritage Site|World Heritage Sites]], mangrove forests and beaches. The Tamil film industry, nicknamed Kollywood, is influential in popular culture.

[[Dravidian languages|Dravidian]] language spoken by the Tamil people of South Asia, concentrated in [[Tamil Nadu]] and [[Pondicherry]] in India and in the Northern and Eastern Provinces of [[Sri Lanka]]. It is one of the longest-surviving classical languages, attested since c. 300 BCE, and Sangam literature includes over 2,000 poems. Tamil was the lingua franca of early maritime traders in South India, and inscriptions in Tamil have been found in Indonesia, Thailand and Egypt. It is an official language in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Sri Lanka and [[Singapore]]. The closest major relative of Tamil is [[Malayalam]], with which it began diverging around the 9th century CE. The Indian government first recognized Tamil as a classical language in 2004.
